messages:
maria: Hey team — customer acme-inc hit a massive burst this morning and started getting 429s. They say it was a short spike (about 30s) but their clients report errors for ~3 min. Attached headers look like rate-limit and burst credits went to 0. Can someone triage?

sam: timeline? did they hit quota or just burst credit exhaustion?

maria: Root message from their side: sudden ramp from 50rps to 8k rps for ~20–30s. They've got a Dedicated plan: reserve 2000rps, burst enabled. Our headers in their logs: `x-rw-rate-limit-remaining: 0`, `x-rw-burst-credits: 0` then 429s.

max (platform): Do we have their burst policy settings on file? I can check config but last commit shows default smoothing window = 60s and max burst = 3x reserve. If they hit 8k while reserve 2k, 3x would allow 6k only — so that would explain 429.

ingrid (sre): @max can you paste the exact policy values from the console? Also any autoscale events?

max (platform): Pulling from console:
```
customer: acme-inc
reserved_rps: 2000
burst_multiplier: 3.0
burst_window_sec: 60
smoothing_policy: token_bucket
burst_credits_total: 6000
burst_credits_replenish_rate_per_sec: 100
```
No autoscale triggers during that minute, infra was healthy.

ops_jen: So if they used 8k rps, 2000 reserved + 6000 burst credits = 8000 total allowed — that exactly exhausts credits and then additional requests got 429. If the spike sustained slightly longer, they dip into 429s while credits refill slowly (`+100/s`).

maria: Customer insists they only had a very short blip and shouldn't have seen errors — they expected smoothing to let short spikes through. Can we explain how burst credits and smoothing interact?

ingrid (sre): Quick explainer for support thread: We use a token-bucket style burst system. Reserved throughput is always available. Burst credits accumulate up to `burst_credits_total` and are consumed when incoming rate > reserved. If consumption > replenish rate then credits deplete and requests above reserved get 429 until credits refill. The smoothing window influences client-side enforcement: a short smoothing window allows more immediate bursts, but the bucket size still caps total.

sam: So the observable behavior: a 30s spike to 8k will consume ~ (8k-2k)*30 = 180k credit-seconds — but our credits are expressed differently; simplified: credits allow 6k extra rps for 1s -> 6000 credits initial then replenish 100/s. They exhausted in seconds and 429s followed.

maria: Ok — customer wants recommendations: 1) How to avoid 429s for short spikes? 2) Any temporary fixes we can apply? 3) Longer-term config suggestions?

max (platform): Recommendations:
- Short term: increase burst_multiplier for their Dedicated pool (eg 4x -> allows 8k). or increase `burst_credits_total`. Both require infra approval for capacity — can do a one-off increase.
- Immediate mitigation: enable client-side smoothing/backoff guidance: cap client concurrency, add jittered exponential backoff for 429s, throttle to 3k–4k rps at client side if they know bursts common.
- Long term: if traffic patterns have frequent spikes, bump reserved capacity or enable autoscale with faster warm-up.

ingrid (sre): Also tell them to set `smoothing_policy` to allow a slightly larger window (e.g., 120s) so sudden peaks spread out from client-side SDKs that honor smoothing. But note: server-side bucket size still caps absolute allowed tokens.

maria: Can we propose a one-off change so I can offer them a remediation while we schedule a proper capacity review?

max (platform): I can approve a temporary bump to burst_multiplier=4 and burst_credits_total=8000 for 24 hours. Need ops_jen to confirm no infra contention.

ops_jen: 24h bump ok for Dedicated cluster A (their tenant in cluster-a). No infra risk. I'll apply change now.

maria: Thanks. I emailed acme-inc and told them we're applying a temporary bump and we'll follow up with recommended client changes. They asked for repro steps so they can validate after we change.

ingrid (sre): Repro steps for customer to validate smoothing/burst behavior:
1) Start a baseline at 2k rps for 60s.
2) Spike to 8k rps for 30s.
3) Hold at 10k rps for 10s to see 429s if over capacity.
4) Capture headers on failure responses (important): `x-rw-rate-limit-remaining`, `x-rw-burst-credits`, `x-rw-retry-after`

Example curl for header capture: 
```bash
for i in {1..1000}; do curl -sI -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate" | head -n 20 >> headers.log; done
```
Note: use a small parallel client to simulate concurrency.

sam: Also provide them a test script (python) that ramps according to pattern and prints per-request status codes and those headers.

maria: I added a support note to the ticket with the bump window and repro steps. Customer will run the test at 17:30 UTC. I'll post results.

billing-bot: Reminder: temporary config change may alter billing if it results in sustained higher token consumption. Please confirm permission from account owner.

maria: @billing-bot noted — emailed billing contact at acme-inc, they approved temporary bump for verification, not for long-term billing increases.

ops_jen: Change applied on cluster-a at 1769813000. New policy values: `burst_multiplier=4`, `burst_credits_total=8000`, `replenish_rate=100/s`.

maria: Customer ran their test: initial spike to 8k succeeded, no 429s during the 30s window, only a few 429s when they held at 10k for 10s. They sent logs with headers showing `x-rw-burst-credits` dropping from 8000 -> ~0 and then slowly refill.

ingrid (sre): Good. Follow-ups: 1) Schedule a capacity review with acme-inc to set a proper reserved RPS or autoscale. 2) Send client SDK guidance to smooth bursts and implement retry/backoff. 3) Consider exposing a per-tenant burst dashboard so customers can see credit balances in Console.

maria: I'll draft a guidance doc (short) and link to SDK examples. Anything else?

max (platform): One more note for support text: clearly explain that "smoothing" doesn't create infinite headroom; it only evens out the surface area of spikes. The hard cap is reserved + burst bucket. Also recommend they instrument token consumption in their app to surface near-exhaustion alerts.

maria: Great — I'll close the loop once doc + ticketing actions are scheduled. :thumbsup:

ops_jen: Marking support ticket as "mitigated (temp bump)" and scheduling follow-up for capacity review.

maria: Closing thread here. Thanks all!
